about: How AI sees a photo (Claude, scoped). Factory #20, backlog row 21, playlist How AI works. One hard idea: Claude takes in a photo as 28-pixel squares, each one a token counted like the words you type, and every photo has a cap on squares, so a 12-megapixel photo is shrunk to under a third of its pixels first (about 4,740 squares on Claude 4.7 and later), which can make small text hard to read. Source sentences: Claude Vision docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision, read 2026-11-03): 'Claude processes images in patches instead of pixels. Each patch is a 28x28-pixel block of the image, referred to as a visual token.' 'Images larger than either limit are downscaled before processing'; limits 2,576 px / 4,784 visual tokens (Claude 4.7 and later), 1,568 px / 1,568 tokens (all other models); 'To estimate cost, multiply the token count by the per-token price of the model'; resizing 'might, for example, make text less legible'; 'If the image contains important text, make sure it's legible and not too small.' Derived with the docs' own resize code: 4032x3024 (12.19 MP) -> 2212x1659 = 79 x 60 = 4,740 visual tokens, 30.1% of the pixels (high-resolution tier); 1270x952 = 1,564 tokens, 9.9% (standard tier). Background idea, not claimed as Claude's design: Dosovitskiy et al. 2020, 'An Image is Worth 16x16 Words' (Google Research, arXiv 2010.11929): 'Image patches are treated the same way as tokens (words) in an NLP application.' Hero: the paper print cut into a square grid, coral stamp 4,740 SQUARES in the 1.3 s silence after 'squares.' Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times. No AI tag anywhere (Isac, 2026-11-03).

lines.text: Your photo? Claude shrinks it first.
It cuts that to under a third.
So why throw the rest away?
Because it works in squares, not pixels.

lines.say: Each twenty-eight pixel square is one token.

lines.text: Counted like the words you type.
And every photo has a token cap.
On newer models, your photo is about 4,700 squares.
lines.say: On newer models, your photo is about forty-seven hundred squares.

lines.text: So small text might get hard to read.
Reading fine print? Get closer first.
Did you know it shrinks your photos? Yes or no.
